verdicts.new_smcl: {phang}{opt adv:ersarial}: Tests the joint hypothesis that all estimated relative time period-specific effects fall on a single line through the reference period, with the slope that fits them best. This null is adversarial toward finding pre-trend violations. The p-value comes from a minimum-distance test on the event-study coefficients and their covariance matrix. Requires {it:esfixedbaseperiod}. The default pooled reference period has no single omitted period, so there the test fails with a caution and nothing is returned. Under {it:timetrends} two periods are normalized to zero and the null reduces to every coefficient being zero. Beside each p-value, {it:wooldid} returns the unweighted OLS line through the coefficients, with 0 at the reference period. The test is cancelled with a caution when the window holds fewer than one pre-treatment and one post-treatment horizon, or fewer than three coefficients in all under {it:timetrends}, when the sample fails to realize those horizons, or when the event-study covariance is degenerate. Under {it:subgroups()} the {it:att} and {it:att_it} tests are skipped for any subgroup that lost a relative period as inestimable. A rank-deficient but not degenerate covariance gives a test at reduced rank, and without {it:bootstrap()} or {it:permute()} a caution gives the rank and the degrees of freedom used. The numerator degrees of freedom are stored in {it:e(adversarial_df_att)} and its twins. Like {it:jointtests}, the test is severely oversized unless many clusters span each treated cohort-by-period cell, which clustering on {it:i} never gives. There, use {it:permute()}, or {it:bootstrap()} with {it:boottstat}. Without {it:boottstat} the test is absent under {it:bootstrap()}. Refused with {it:impvalues}, and with {it:fastnose} except under {it:permute()}. {p_end}

verdicts.new_smcl: {pstd} A fixed reference period is transparent: every cohort is compared to the same relative period. A pooled one can be more precise, since it averages over more periods, but different cohorts' reference periods then hold different numbers of periods. A pooled period is likely a poor choice when treated cohorts' outcomes evolve differently from the comparison cohorts' before treatment. Trends shared by all cohorts are absorbed by the time fixed effects. It also tends to be a poor choice when requesting more pre-treatment horizons than every cohort can supply. A cohort with fewer observed pre-treatment periods then takes its earliest observed period as its reference period, even where other cohorts report an effect for that period. With differing outcome trends, the event study can then show counterintuitive time paths that hide even severe parallel trends violations. {p_end}

verdicts.new_smcl: {phang}{opt sub:groups()}: Specifies the subgroup (SG) variable, whose levels define the subgroups for which {it:wooldid} computes separate estimates. The SG variable must hold non-negative integers or missing values on the observations of treated units, and its levels must be collections of cohorts i. Observations with missing values belong to no subgroup and are ignored in subgroup computations. A unit is left out only if it is missing on all of its rows. A treated unit split across subgroups, or labelled on some rows and missing on others, is refused. With {it:safety(off)}, except under {it:permute()}, such a unit enters each of its subgroups weighted by its labelled share of sample weight there, under a caution. A split unit then no longer carries equal weight in {it:att_i} and {it:att_itime}. Subgroup values are embedded in the names of stored results and plots, so values 8 or more digits long can exceed Stata's limits on names. Recode ID-style codes to small integers first, for example with {it:egen newsg = group(oldsg)}. With {it:esprelength()} greater than 0, an {it:espostlength()} of 0 is raised to 1 under a caution (see {it:espostlength()}). Not compatible with {it:impvalues}. {p_end}
